ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, two right-angled triangles $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle BCD$ are placed as shown in the figure, with $\angle BCA=45^\circ$, $\angle D=30^\circ$, and the two hypotenuses intersecting at point O. What is the ratio of the areas of $\triangle AOB$ to $\triangle COD$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $BC=x$,\\
In right triangle $\triangle ABC$,\\
$\because$ $\angle BCA=45^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \tan \angle BCA = \frac{AB}{BC}$,\\
$\therefore AB=BC=x$,\\
In right triangle $\triangle BCD$, $\angle D=30^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \tan D = \frac{BC}{DC}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$,\\
$\therefore DC= \sqrt{3}BC=\sqrt{3}x$,\\
Furthermore, $\because AB\parallel CD$,\\
$\therefore \triangle AOB \sim \triangle COD$,\\
$\therefore \frac{S_{\triangle AOB}}{S_{\triangle COD}}=\left(\frac{AB}{CD}\right)^2=\left(\frac{x}{\sqrt{3}x}\right)^2=\boxed{\frac{1}{3}}$,\\

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: The diagram shows B and C on the bottom segment BC. Segment AB rises from B and is marked perpendicular to BC, forming right triangle ABC. Segment CD rises from C and is marked perpendicular to BC, forming right triangle BCD. The two slanted hypotenuse segments AC and BD cross at O inside the figure. The given angles are ∠BCA=45° and ∠D=30°. Reasoning: Let BC=x. In right triangle ABC, the angle at C is 45°, so tan∠BCA=AB/BC. Since tan45°=1, AB=BC=x. In right triangle BCD, the right angle is at C and ∠D=30°, so tan30°=BC/CD=√3/3. Therefore CD=√3·BC=√3x. Because AB and CD are both perpendicular to BC, AB∥CD. Since AC and BD intersect at O, ∠AOB and ∠COD are vertical angles, and the other corresponding angles are equal due to AB∥CD. Thus △AOB∼△COD. The ratio of their areas equals the square of the ratio of corresponding sides: S△AOB/S△COD=(AB/CD)^2=(x/(√3x))^2=1/3.
